sentence_stem: If I had known about the traffic jam,
correct_completion: I would have taken the train.
full_sentence: If I had known about the traffic jam, I would have taken the train.
acceptable_variants: I would have called a taxi.
I would have left home earlier.

options.text: I would take the train tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This uses a present or future form, but the stem refers to an unreal past situation, so a past result is needed.

options.text: I took the train every day.
options.why_wrong: This describes a past habit but does not give the imagined result of the unreal past condition.

options.text: I would have taken the train.
I will be late for work.
options.why_wrong: This states a real future consequence, not an imagined past result, so it does not match the third conditional.

grammar_focus: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle
explanation: The third conditional describes an imagined past situation and its imagined past result. Learners often use a simple past or would alone here, because Portuguese speakers may transfer a single past form instead of using had + past participle in the condition and would have + past participle in the result.
translation: Se eu tivesse sabido do congestionamento, teria pegado o trem.
